why: `pop()` reads from the bottom of the stack with `shift()`, so Back closes the layer UNDER the one on screen: with Records open over Settings the player's Back dismisses Settings while Records stays, and a confirmation's Back removes the route it was raised over while the confirmation stays up. A plain LIFO pop is the entire mechanism behind the issue's "Back removes one overlay before one route", so this is the mutation that breaks that guarantee directly. Fails 2 of 15 in navigation.test.ts: `back pops the topmost layer, LIFO: [route a, route b] pops b then a` and `an overlay above a route is removed before the route, and each pop carries its own recorded origin and restore`, each at its first `pop()` assertion.

The refusal that keeps a full-screen destination from opening under a modal is deleted, so a route push while a confirmation is up succeeds: the Levels grid opens over the dialog the player was answering, and the next Back closes the grid and drops the player back INTO a confirmation they had already navigated away from. The LIFO order the module claims by construction (an overlay is always above every route) stops being true. Fails 1 of 15 in navigation.test.ts: `a route pushed over an open overlay is refused and the stack is unchanged`, at its `'refused'` assertion. The overlay-over-overlay control in the same case still passes, which is what shows the assertion is about the route/overlay pairing and not about any push over an overlay.

The already-top check is deleted, so re-opening the layer already on screen falls through to the open-lower-down scan and is reported `refused` instead of `already-top`. The owner branches on that result -- `already-top` re-renders the current layer in place, `refused` is a failed open -- so a second press of the control that opened the Records page would do nothing rather than refresh it. The stack is unchanged under either code, which is why only the result code can see this. Fails 1 of 15 in navigation.test.ts: `pushing the id already on top reports already-top and pushes nothing; an id open lower down is refused`.

`sync(d>0)` pushes the sentinel from `present` as well as from `absent`, which turns the single-entry design into an entry per layer AND a further entry per in-app pop that leaves layers open. The player then presses the browser's Back once per pushed entry to leave, and the traversals the design bounds to one at a time pile up. Fails 3 of 15 in navigation.test.ts: `the first layer pushes exactly one sentinel and a second layer pushes none`, `an in-app pop with a layer remaining touches history not at all; emptying the stack retires the sentinel with one back()`, and `a browser Back at depth 2 pops one layer and re-pushes the sentinel through the re-entrant sync; at depth 1 pops one and pushes nothing`, each at an exact `host.calls` list.
